# Edinburgh（爱丁堡）

Edinburgh splits cleanly into Old Town (castle, Royal Mile, closely
packed sights) and a wider ring of parks, museums, and villages a short
bus or taxi ride out — a good structure for spreading a multi-day trip
across distinct areas without much backtracking.

## Must-See

### Edinburgh Castle（Edinburgh Castle）

Sits on an extinct volcanic plug above the city, visible from most of
Old Town. Home to the Scottish Crown Jewels and the Stone of Destiny.
Queues build quickly once tour buses arrive.

- **Category / area:** castle / landmark — Old Town
- **Reservation:** required (timed entry)
- **Hours:** 09:30–17:00
- **Source:** https://example.com/edinburgh-castle-hours (checked 2026-08-01)

### Royal Mile（Royal Mile）

The historic spine connecting the Castle to Holyrood Palace, lined with
closes (narrow alleys), shops, and street performers.

- **Category / area:** street / district — Old Town
- **Reservation:** not_needed
- **Hours:** open at all times (shops vary)
- **Source:** https://example.com/royal-mile (checked 2026-08-01)

### Arthur's Seat（Arthur's Seat）

An extinct volcano within Holyrood Park, the highest point in
Edinburgh. The summit route is a genuine hike; shorter viewpoint paths
exist from the Dunsapie Loch car park.

- **Category / area:** landscape / hike — Holyrood Park
- **Reservation:** not_needed
- **Hours:** park open dawn to dusk
- **Source:** https://example.com/arthurs-seat (checked 2026-08-01)

## Recommended

### National Museum of Scotland（National Museum of Scotland）

Free entry, broad collection spanning natural history, world cultures,
and Scottish history — a reliable indoor option regardless of weather.

- **Category / area:** museum — Southside
- **Reservation:** not_needed
- **Hours:** 10:00–17:00
- **Cost:** 0 GBP
- **Source:** https://example.com/national-museum-scotland (checked 2026-08-01)

### Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh（Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh）

70 acres of gardens and glasshouses, a short bus ride from Old Town.
Calm and low-effort compared to the city-centre sights.

- **Category / area:** garden — Inverleith
- **Reservation:** not_needed
- **Hours:** 10:00–17:00
- **Cost:** 0 GBP (glasshouses extra)
- **Source:** https://example.com/royal-botanic-garden (checked 2026-08-01)

## Optional

### Camera Obscura & World of Illusions（Camera Obscura）

An interactive, family-oriented attraction right by the Castle
esplanade — optical illusions and a rooftop terrace view.

- **Category / area:** attraction — Old Town
- **Reservation:** recommended
- **Hours:** 09:30–19:00 (last admission 18:00)
- **Cost:** 20.50 GBP
- **Source:** https://example.com/camera-obscura (checked 2026-05-02, unverified — 3-month-old source)

### Dean Village（Dean Village）

A quiet former mill village on the Water of Leith, a well-known photo
spot, about 40 minutes' walk from Old Town.

- **Category / area:** neighborhood — West End
- **Reservation:** not_needed
- **Hours:** open at all times
- **Source:** https://example.com/dean-village (checked 2026-08-01)

## Cost-Saving Tips

- The National Museum of Scotland and the Royal Botanic Garden's outdoor
  areas are both free — good anchors for a mid-range budget.
- Booking Edinburgh Castle online in advance is both cheaper and avoids
  the walk-up queue.

## General Notes

- Arthur's Seat's summit path involves loose gravel and no barriers near
  the top — not recommended for young children; the Dunsapie Loch
  viewpoint path is a gentler alternative.
